# 什么是零号位？

- 原标题：What Is Position Zero?
- 作者：Flavio Amiel Roborank 创始人
- 原文更新日期：2026-07-15
- 原文：https://roborank.io/glossary/position-zero/
- 栏目：[AI Search & GEO](https://roborank.io/ai-search/)
- 说明：中文全文翻译，后附英文原文。原文中的数据、观点、平台说明及推广内容均按原文保留，未经独立验证。

---

## 中文全文

零号位（Position Zero）是 SEO 行业对精选摘要的非正式称呼，指过去出现在第一条自然搜索结果上方的引用式答案框，仿佛排在第一名“之前”。这个昵称早于 Google 在 2020 年作出的调整：Google 不再在普通结果列表中重复显示已进入摘要的页面，将该位置并入第一名，而不是把它作为独立位置。

### 核心要点

- “零号位”是行业术语，不是 Google 的正式用语；它描述精选摘要位于第一条蓝色链接上方的展示位置。
- 2020 年 1 月 22 日，Google 宣布，出现在精选摘要中的页面，不再重复出现在下方的自然搜索结果里。
- 去重调整之后，在 Search Console 报告中，Google 将精选摘要视为第一名，而不是独立的零号位。
- 获得这一位置可能提高某些查询的点击率，但也会促成另一些查询的零点击搜索，因为答案框可能已经完全满足搜索者。
- 精选摘要出现时，每个查询只有一个，因此零号位是一个只有一位赢家的位置，不是一份排名列表。

### 零号位如何运作

零号位描述的是展示位置，而不是一种机制。当 Google 判断直接答案最适合满足某个查询时，会从已有排名的页面中提取一段文字，将其提升为结果最顶部带框的[精选摘要](https://roborank.io/glossary/featured-snippet/)，位于第一条自然搜索链接上方，而且通常也在广告上方。因为它出现在第一名“之前”，SEO 社区开始称其为零号位。Google 从未使用过这个术语，其文档始终称这一元素为精选摘要。

这个位置只有一位赢家。对于一个查询，Google 最多展示一个精选摘要，来源是一个页面。因此，零号位与排名列表不同：你不能逐级爬进去，答案框内部也没有“第二名”。Google 会选择段落最清楚、最直接回答具体问题的页面，因此[答案优先写作](https://roborank.io/glossary/answer-first-writing/)和真正具有[可提取性](https://roborank.io/glossary/extractability/)的段落，比单纯的权威性更重要。一个自然排名第四或第五的页面，如果拥有最简明的答案，也仍然可以占据摘要位置。

2020 年初，其运作机制发生了重要变化，这也是如今“零”这一称呼在技术上不准确的原因。在此之前，一个页面可能在第一页出现两次：一次在精选摘要中，一次在通常的自然排名位置。Google 终止了这种重复。现在，摘要来源页面只展示一次，Google 将摘要报告为第一名。因此，如今更准确的理解是“附带突出答案的第一名”，而不是高于列表的一个独立排名。

### 零号位示例

这个术语历史上记录最充分的事件，是 Google 对精选摘要进行去重。Google 的公开 Search Liaison 账号于 **2020 年 1 月 22 日**宣布此事，[Search Engine Journal](https://www.searchenginejournal.com/google-featured-snippets-guidance/344972/) 作了详细报道。调整之前，一个进入精选摘要的 URL，经常还会在第一页更靠下的位置再次出现：页面同时占据“零号位”和一个普通自然结果位置。

Google 对解决方案的描述很直接：如果一个网页结果被提升至精选摘要位置，它就不再在搜索结果中重复出现，这样可以“让结果更整洁，帮助用户更容易找到相关信息”。Google 还解释了报告机制：它只把 URL 最靠上的一次出现记录为排名，而精选摘要*此前就已经*被计为第一名；调整只是停止展示靠下的重复结果。实际来说，一个原本排名第一、后来又获得摘要的页面，会保留摘要，失去第二条冗余结果；一个自然排名并非第一但赢得摘要的页面，则会让原先靠下的条目完全退出第一页。

其中的道理明确，而且至今适用。零号位中的“零”，始终只是对屏幕位置的描述，从不是 Google 授予的排名。去重后，Google 自己将该位置并入第一名，因此把它当作独立、更高层级去追逐，误读了搜索结果页面的实际运作方式。真正长期有效的是它背后的写作检验：Google 把答案框给到那个用一个段落最清楚回答查询的页面——同样的标准也决定[其他人还问](https://roborank.io/glossary/people-also-ask/)中的答案，并越来越多地为 [AI 概览](https://roborank.io/glossary/ai-overviews/)提供内容。

### 人们常犯的错误

人们的错误，是追逐“零号位”，仿佛它是一个高于第一名、爬上去就能永久占有的排名。它从来不是排名，而是 Google 授予最清楚回答查询的那个页面的独立答案框；Google 随时都可能撤回它、改写文字或更换来源。自 2020 年去重调整以来，称其为“零”在技术上就不正确——Google 现在将它计为第一名。我仍然使用这个词，因为客户熟悉它，但我会指导团队不要再把它当成奖杯，而要把它当成写作测试：你的页面里，是否有一个段落能如此直白地回答具体问题，以至于 Google 愿意在自己的结果页上引用它？如果没有，再多的链接建设也无法把你送进答案框。

### 零号位与精选摘要

|  | 零号位 | 精选摘要 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **是什么** | SEO 行业对该位置的非正式昵称 | Google 对该元素的正式名称 |
| **名称来源** | 它位于第一条自然结果上方 | Google 搜索文档 |
| **如今是否准确** | 已过时——Google 现在将其计为第一名 | 仍然准确，且是现行名称 |
| **指代对象** | 同一个答案框 | 同一个答案框 |

两个术语指向同一个功能。“精选摘要”是 Google 的称呼，也出现在其文档和报告中；“零号位”则是社区沿用的简称，因为这个框曾经位于最高排名链接上方。需要精确表达时，使用“精选摘要”，并记住该位置现在报告为第一名，而非独立排名。

### 常见问题

#### SEO 中的零号位是什么？

零号位是 Google 精选摘要的非正式名称，指过去显示在第一条自然搜索结果上方的引用式答案框。这个昵称反映了它位于第一名“之前”的位置，尽管 Google 从未正式使用过该术语。

#### 零号位现在还存在吗？

功能还存在，但名称已经过时。Google 在 2020 年 1 月进行去重调整后，精选摘要来源页面不再同时出现在自然结果列表中，Google 也将摘要计为第一名。答案框仍然存在；“零”这个编号已经不符合 Google 的报告方式。

#### 零号位和精选摘要有什么区别？

实际没有区别。“精选摘要”是 Google 对答案框的名称；“零号位”是 SEO 社区基于它位于最高自然结果上方而起的昵称。两者指的是同一个搜索结果页元素。

#### 零号位会增加流量吗？

取决于查询。对于需要更多细节的问题，占据摘要可能提高点击率；但对于简单的事实性问题，答案框往往直接满足搜索者，带来零点击搜索。即使获得可见性，也不一定有访问。

### 结论

零号位是昵称，不是一个排名层级：它指的是精选摘要，即 Google 放在结果顶部、唯一的引用式答案框。这个词沿用至今，是因为答案框曾位于第一条链接上方；但 Google 在 2020 年停止重复展示摘要来源页面后，这个位置最好理解为带有答案的第一名。要争取它，应写出对问题最清楚的那个答案，而不是试图爬到列表之上一个想象出来的排名。

## 英文原文

Position Zero is the informal SEO name for the featured snippet — the quoted answer box that historically appeared above the first organic result, effectively ranking “before” position one. The nickname predates a 2020 Google change that stopped repeating a snippet page in the regular listings, folding the slot into position one rather than a spot of its own.

### Key Takeaways

- “Position Zero” is industry jargon, not a Google term; it describes the featured snippet’s placement above the #1 blue link.
- On January 22, 2020, Google announced that a page shown in the featured snippet is no longer repeated in the organic results below it.
- After that deduplication change, Google treats the featured snippet as position one, not a separate position zero, in Search Console reporting.
- Winning the slot can lift click-through on some queries but fuels zero-click searches on others, since the boxed answer may fully satisfy the searcher.
- There is exactly one featured snippet per query when it appears, making position zero a single-winner slot rather than a ranked list.

### How Position Zero Works

Position Zero describes a placement, not a mechanism. When Google decides a query is best served by a direct answer, it promotes one passage from a ranking page into a boxed [featured snippet](https://roborank.io/glossary/featured-snippet/) at the very top of the results — above the first organic link, and often above the ads. Because it sits “before” the #1 result, the SEO community started calling it position zero. Google has never used that term; its documentation only ever calls the element a featured snippet.

The slot is single-winner. For a given query, Google shows at most one featured snippet, sourced from one page. That makes position zero unlike a ranked list: you do not climb into it incrementally, and there is no “second place” inside the box. Google selects the page whose passage answers the exact question most cleanly, which is why [answer-first writing](https://roborank.io/glossary/answer-first-writing/) and a genuinely [extractable](https://roborank.io/glossary/extractability/) passage matter more than raw authority. A page ranking fourth or fifth organically can still hold the snippet if its answer is the crispest one available.

The mechanics changed meaningfully in early 2020, and the change is why the “zero” label is now technically inaccurate. Before then, a page could appear twice on page one: once in the snippet and again in its normal organic spot. Google ended that. A snippet page is now shown once, and Google reports the snippet as position one. So the modern reality is closer to “position one, with the answer surfaced” than a distinct rank sitting above the list.

### Example of Position Zero

The best-documented event in the term’s history is Google’s featured-snippet deduplication, announced by Google’s public Search Liaison on **January 22, 2020** and covered in detail by [Search Engine Journal](https://www.searchenginejournal.com/google-featured-snippets-guidance/344972/). Before the change, a URL elevated into the featured snippet frequently also appeared again lower on the first page — the page occupied both “position zero” and a normal organic slot.

Google’s stated fix was blunt: if a web page listing is elevated into the featured snippet position, it is no longer repeated in the search results, which “declutters the results and helps users locate relevant information more easily.” Google also clarified the reporting side, noting that it logs only the topmost appearance of a URL as its position, and that featured snippets were *already* counted as position one — duplicate lower appearances simply stopped being shown. In practical terms, a page that had been ranking #1 and then won the snippet kept the snippet but lost its second, redundant listing; a page that won the snippet without ranking #1 organically saw its lower listing pushed off page one entirely.

The lesson is precise and still current. The “zero” in position zero was always a description of screen placement, never a ranking Google awarded. After deduplication, Google itself folded the slot into position one, so treating it as a separate, higher tier to chase misreads how the results page actually works. The durable takeaway is the writing test underneath it: Google gives the box to the single page whose passage most cleanly answers the query — the same standard that decides [People Also Ask](https://roborank.io/glossary/people-also-ask/) answers and increasingly feeds [AI Overviews](https://roborank.io/glossary/ai-overviews/).

### The thing people get wrong

What people get wrong is chasing "position zero" as if it were a permanent, higher-than-first rank you climb to and keep. It was never a rank. It is a single answer box Google grants to the one page that most cleanly answers the query, and Google can revoke it, reword it, or replace the source on any given day. Since the 2020 deduplication change, calling it "zero" is technically wrong — Google now counts it as position one. I still use the phrase because clients know it, but I coach teams to stop treating it as a trophy and start treating it as a writing test: can one passage on your page answer the exact question so plainly that Google would stake its own results page on quoting it? If not, no amount of link building moves you into the box.

### Position Zero vs Featured Snippet

|  | Position Zero | Featured Snippet |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **What it is** | Informal SEO nickname for the slot | Google’s official name for the element |
| **Origin of the name** | Its placement above the #1 organic result | Google Search documentation |
| **Accuracy today** | Dated — Google now counts it as position one | Current and correct |
| **Refers to** | The same answer box | The same answer box |

The two terms point at one feature. “Featured snippet” is what Google calls it and what shows in its docs and reports; “position zero” is the community shorthand that stuck because the box once sat above the top link. Use “featured snippet” when precision matters, and remember the slot is now reported as position one rather than a rank of its own.

### Frequently Asked Questions

#### What is Position Zero in SEO?

Position Zero is the informal name for Google’s featured snippet — the quoted answer box that historically appeared above the first organic result. The nickname reflects its placement “before” position one, though Google itself has never used the term officially.

#### Is Position Zero still a thing?

The feature is, but the label is dated. Since Google’s January 2020 deduplication change, a featured snippet page no longer also appears in the organic list, and Google counts the snippet as position one. The answer box remains; the “zero” numbering no longer reflects how Google reports it.

#### What is the difference between Position Zero and a featured snippet?

There is none in practice. “Featured snippet” is Google’s name for the answer box; “Position Zero” is the SEO community’s nickname for the same feature, based on its placement above the top organic result. They refer to the identical SERP element.

#### Does Position Zero increase traffic?

It depends on the query. Owning the snippet can raise click-through for questions that need more detail, but for simple factual questions the boxed answer often satisfies the searcher in place, producing a zero-click search and no visit despite the visibility.

### The Bottom Line

Position Zero is a nickname, not a ranking tier: it points at the featured snippet, the lone quoted answer box Google places at the top of results. The term stuck because the box once sat above the #1 link, but after Google stopped duplicating snippet pages in 2020, the slot is best understood as position one with an answer attached. Earn it by writing the single cleanest answer to the question, not by climbing to an imaginary rank above the list.
